children: Texmaco’s quarterly revenue rises sequentially, but lower Indian Railways orders weigh on annual revenue and profit, while the company expands its private and export customer base

Texmaco Rail & Engineering's revenue from operations fell 31.3 per cent year on year to Rs 863 crore in the second quarter of FY27, as lower orders from Indian Railways weighed on its core business. Profit after tax (PAT) declined 41.6 per cent to Rs 36 crore from Rs 62 crore in the year-ago quarter.
Quarterly revenue, however, rose 14.6 per cent from Rs 753 crore in the first quarter of FY27. Profit before tax increased 15.9 per cent sequentially to Rs 51.2 crore from Rs 44.1 crore.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) stood at Rs 88 crore in Q2 FY27, against Rs 137 crore in the year-ago quarter and Rs 81 crore in Q1. The Ebitda margin stood at 10.2 per cent, compared with 10.9 per cent in Q2 FY26 and 10.8 per cent in Q1 FY27.

The decline in annual revenue came as Texmaco faced lower freight car orders from Indian Railways. The company said its freight car business recorded a 3.8 per cent sequential increase in revenue during the quarter, while Railway Infrastructure revenue rose 41.7 per cent and Infrastructure Electrical revenue increased 38 per cent.
The sequential recovery did not offset the lower revenue base compared with the corresponding quarter last year. Texmaco sold 1,106 wagons during Q2 FY27.

The company has sought to offset the decline in Indian Railways orders through private-sector and export markets. Its management said the company has expanded its customer base beyond Indian Railways, with freight car demand from overseas markets and orders from private domestic customers forming part of the strategy.

The shift in customer mix has become more pronounced as Indian Railways orders have declined. The company said the reduction in railway orders has prompted a greater focus on private and export markets, along with rail infrastructure, electrification and other businesses.

The change in order composition gives Texmaco a different revenue base from previous years, but the Q2 numbers show that lower Indian Railways order flow continues to affect the company’s annual financial performance.
Texmaco also secured fresh orders after the end of the quarter. The company received a Rs 412 crore freight car order from Indian Railways after 30 September, according to its management commentary.

The company has also reported traction from private-sector customers and export markets as it seeks to reduce its dependence on Indian Railways. The immediate challenge remains the conversion of this changing order mix into higher revenue and profitability after the year-on-year decline recorded in Q2 FY27.
